title: Stimulating other nodes can break pharmacoresistance in many pathway models

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stimulating other nodes can break pharmacoresistance in many pathway models

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In 17 of the 27 habituating BioModels pathway models (about 63%), stimulating a third node (neither the stimulus nor the response) abolished habituation for some stimulus–response pairs, so some biological networks contain discoverable stimulus nodes that may serve to break pharmacoresistance without rewiring the network.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Overall, we conclude that in some biological networks, there are discoverable stimulus nodes that may serve towards breaking pharmacoresistance.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance”. Scope: 27 habituating ODE pathway models from BioModels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-16: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.91

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a finite computational search with a clear intervention and binary outcome. It can be reproduced directly from existing public models.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For every habituating pair, stimulate each eligible third node and retest the 50% habituation criterion. Count models with at least one successful break and compare with 17 of 27.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Threshold-sensitive pairs may change classification.

A successful model node may not correspond to a feasible biological intervention.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.94
operationalizability: 0.97
data adequacy: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.82
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The breaking rule, the three-trial cap and the 27-model base are specified, and the repository includes the breaking analysis. Re-running it decides whether about 63 percent of the habituating models contain at least one effective third node. That is the claim's actual scope; the therapeutic wording is carried by the same in silico count.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After establishing habituation, stimulate each third node for up to three trials and count a model as breakable if any stimulus–response pair loses the 50 percent decline. Breaks in 17 of 27 models would confirm the count; a substantially different model count would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: A third-node clamp in an ODE is not yet a deliverable drug stimulus in cells.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9
data existence: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.58
